body:
I need drafted dialogue for a small group of scenes in a single-player D&D Curse of Strahd game. Plain text only (no JSON, no markdown tables), nodes under `~ name`, one line per row as `Speaker [mood]: Text`, ASCII only (straight quotes and apostrophes, no accents or fancy dashes, no em-dash: use a comma or a full stop), 1-2 sentences a line, nothing over about 28 words, no placeholders like {name}. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

## The situation

Ireena Kolyana (a proud, red-haired young woman, the dead burgomaster's adopted daughter, twice bitten by Strahd) has been left by the party to shelter somewhere: the Blue Water Inn or St. Andral's church in Vallaki, a friend's house behind Krezk's wall, or her father's mansion in the village. She does not travel with them now. While the party is away on the road and something big happens that she would hear of, a courier brings the party a letter in her hand. The courier is NEVER named and never described beyond a line: a carter's boy, a Vistani child, a pilgrim, a goatherd. The letter is read aloud as lines spoken by Ireena. She never begs. She is proud, dry and exact, and she says what she wants in the shape of a complaint or an order, because that is how she says anything tender.

The point of the letters is that she is still thinking about them, and that the party owes her a visit. No letter gives quest information, hints at where to go or what to do, or names a place the party must go. No letter says "come back" in a pleading way; the nearest she gets is something like "the shutters are well kept and I have run out of excuses to check them".

Every letter must read right whether she SAW the event or only HEARD of it from carters, Vistani and pilgrims (she is in different places). So write each letter as news that has reached her, not as something she witnessed.

## Nodes to write

COURIERS (Narrator x1 each; the party is on the road and a messenger finds them with a folded letter; second person, present tense, one or two sentences; the courier is not named):
- courier_vallaki: she is at the Blue Water Inn or St. Andral's in Vallaki. The messenger is a carter's boy from the Svalich road.
- courier_krezk: she is behind Krezk's wall. The messenger is a goatherd or a pilgrim from the Krezk road.
- courier_mansion: she is at her father's mansion in the village of Barovia. The messenger is a village child in a too-big coat.

THE SIX LETTERS (Ireena, 3 lines each unless the node says otherwise; these are her letter; no greeting like "Dear", no signature; she writes the way she speaks):
- letter_festival: the festival in Vallaki is over. 2 lines of common letter, then ONE extra line for each outcome:
  - festival_baron: the Baron kept his chair and the town is cheerful at sword-point.
  - festival_wachter: Lady Wachter rules, for the devil, and the festival bunting is gone.
  - festival_neither: no one rules by decree; the priest and the innkeeper keep a council.
- letter_abbot: bats now circle the wall at night, every night, and do not come in. She does not know why. 3 lines.
- letter_den: the werewolf den in the hills is finished one way or another. 2 lines of common letter, then ONE extra line for each:
  - den_emil: the pack's new leader keeps to the hills and leaves the farms alone.
  - den_kiril: the old leader still hunts for the castle.
  - den_none: both leaders are dead and the pack is scattered.
- letter_beacon: a light has been seen burning on the ridge of the old dragon's house, steady and white, and nothing the wind does moves it. 3 lines.
- letter_wine: wine is flowing again from the old winery. Her father bought one cask from that hill every year for her name day, and a cart came with a cask this season and no note. 3 lines.
- letter_dinner: she has heard the party sat at the devil's table. She is not angry, she is exact: she wants to know whether anyone counted the spoons, and says she will want the whole story at a table that does not belong to him. 3 lines.

AFTER THE LETTER (the party's two exits; Narrator x1 each, one sentence):
- after_keep: the party keeps the letter safe in a pack.
- after_tell: the party tells the courier they will come as soon as they can, and the courier nods and goes.

COLD GREETINGS (the party has now come to see her after the letters went unanswered; she opens cold, in person; Ireena x2 each; [angry], [weary], [sad] or no mood in square brackets):
- cold_two: two letters, no word back.
- cold_three: three letters, no word back. One line of hers must be: "Three letters. I was starting to write the fourth to your graves." (use it exactly), then one more.

That is: couriers 3, letters about 22, after 2, cold 4 = about 31 lines.

## Voice reminders

IREENA: direct and proud; short sentences, no ornament; dry humour with an edge; she makes the grim joke before anyone can pity her; never says "please" to Strahd's name; she never says his name at all, she says "him", "the devil" or "our visitor"; gets more formal, not softer, when she grieves. Pet phrases: "I'm not made of glass." "Say it plainly." "Father would want it done properly." Moods allowed: [angry], [sad], [afraid], [smile], [weary]; most lines carry none.
NARRATOR: old gothic storyteller, second person or plain scene description, present tense, one or two sentences, the second a turn; concrete senses; never cruel; no game terms (no "party" in the sense of game mechanics, no "quest").

Some of her existing lines, so you hear her (do NOT repeat them): "Back with all your limbs. Good. Tell me what you stirred up out there." / "The devil is a thing that happens to people, whether they bar the shutters or not." / "Everyone who loves him, or is loved by him, leaves the same kind of ruin." / "I dry glasses until midnight, and then I sit with Urwin while he watches the shutters." / "I sit in Father's chair after the lamps go out and talk to the panelling." / "I'm not made of glass. I'm made of whatever's left when the glass breaks."

## Canon limits

No new named characters (no names for couriers). Do not name Strahd. Do not mention Tatyana, Sergei or her past life. Real places and people you may mention: Vallaki, Urwin Martikov and the Blue Water Inn, Father Lucian and St. Andral's, Krezk and Dmitri and Anna Krezkova's house, her brother Ismark, her father Kolyan, the Wizard of Wines winery, Argynvostholt. Do not invent any other names, numbers, places or history. Do not say the party fought anyone. Do not give directions, ask the party to do anything specific, or hint at quest steps.
result:
~ courier_vallaki
Narrator: A carter's boy flags you down along the muddy ruts from Vallaki, wiping rain from his chin. He presses a folded square of stiff paper into your hand.

~ courier_krezk
Narrator: A grey-cloaked pilgrim coming down the steep track from Krezk stops beside you without a word. From inside his sleeve, he draws a small letter sealed in tallow.

~ courier_mansion
Narrator: A village child in a coat three sizes too large waits by the roadside milestone. She holds out a neat, folded note that smells faintly of old cedar.

~ letter_festival
Ireena: The carters cannot stop talking about the festival in Vallaki, though half of them change the story at every milepost. I assume your boots were somewhere near the ash.
Ireena [weary]: I have mended every cuff I own twice over waiting for a proper account of it.

~ festival_baron
Ireena: They say the Baron still sits in his chair, and the townsfolk are smiling again at the point of a pike.

~ festival_wachter
Ireena [angry]: Word reaches me that the bunting is down and Lady Wachter keeps the town now, quite openly, for the devil.

~ festival_neither
Ireena: Travellers say no lord rules by decree there now, and only Father Lucian and Urwin Martikov keep the peace.

~ letter_abbot
Ireena: The pilgrims say bats circle the high wall every night now, thick as chimney smoke against the clouds. Strange to hear that none of them ever drop inside.
Ireena [afraid]: I do not like mysteries that keep regular hours, and I like them less when they belong to our visitor.
Ireena: The shutters here are well kept, and I have quite run out of excuses to check the latches.

~ letter_den
Ireena: Drovers on the road are swearing that the business at the werewolf den in the hills is finally settled. Nobody seems to know the whole truth of it, which tells me you were involved.
Ireena: You might have sent word yourself instead of letting me hear it over a turnip cart.

~ den_emil
Ireena: They say the pack has a new leader who keeps his teeth to the high timber and leaves the farms alone.

~ den_kiril
Ireena [weary]: Word is the old pack leader still runs the ridges and hunts at the castle's pleasure.

~ den_none
Ireena: The shepherds claim both pack leaders are dead in the dirt and the rest have scattered into the mist.

~ letter_beacon
Ireena: Every peddler on the road has seen the white light burning above Argynvostholt. They say the mountain wind batters the ridge all night and the flame never wavers.
Ireena [smile]: It is a fine thing to hear of a light in this valley that the devil cannot blow out.
Ireena: Come and tell me who lit it before the gossips ruin the story.

~ letter_wine
Ireena: The carts are rolling down from the Wizard of Wines again, and a driver left a single cask by the door with no note. Father bought one from that hill every year for my name day.
Ireena [sad]: Father would want it done properly, and I refuse to drink good vintage alone with the panelling.
Ireena: Bring yourselves back before I am forced to share it with people who do not know its worth.

~ letter_dinner
Ireena [angry]: A Vistani girl told me you sat at the devil's own table and ate off his silver. I am not made of glass, so you need not spare me the details.
Ireena: I only want to know whether any of you had the sense to count the spoons before you left.
Ireena: You owe me the whole story, told plainly, at a table that does not belong to him.

~ after_keep
Narrator: You refold the stiff paper along its sharp creases and tuck it dry inside your pack.

~ after_tell
Narrator: You tell the messenger you will come as soon as the road allows, and with a quiet nod, the figure turns back into the mist.

~ cold_two
Ireena [angry]: Two letters I sent down that road, and not so much as a scrap of charcoal by way of a reply. I was beginning to think you had forgotten how to read my hand.
Ireena [weary]: Sit down and take your cloaks off before you drip all over the floorboards.

~ cold_three
Ireena [angry]: Three letters. I was starting to write the fourth to your graves.
Ireena [sad]: Say it plainly if you mean to vanish again, because I am tired of listening for boots at the gate.
